procedure.description: inpatient admission, septicemia or severe sepsis without mechanical ventilation over 96 hours, with major complication or comorbidity

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for MS-DRG 871 (inpatient admission, septicemia or severe sepsis without mechanical ventilation over 96 hours, with major complication or comorbidity) with dates of service 2026-02-04 through 2026-02-08. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: Inpatient level of care is not supported by the clinical documentation. Observation services were appropriate for the services rendered; the claim is denied as billed.

criteria.text: Sepsis documented by a suspected or confirmed infection with at least two systemic inflammatory response criteria or a qSOFA score of 2 or more, together with evidence of hypoperfusion or organ dysfunction such as a lactate of 2 or more or hypotension.
Treatment required inpatient-level resources: intravenous fluid resuscitation of 30 mL/kg, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, serial lactate measurement, and continuous hemodynamic monitoring.

At the time of the admission order, the admitting physician documented a reasonable expectation that care would span at least two midnights, and the actual stay met that expectation or was shortened by an unforeseen event.
The condition could not be safely treated with outpatient or observation services.

chart.text: 78 year old man brought in by his spouse with two days of fever, chills, and left-sided back pain, poor oral intake since yesterday. History of hypertension and type 2 diabetes.

Admission history and physical. Assessment: pyelonephritis. Plan as above. Family updated at the bedside. 2.5 liters of lactated Ringer’s given as a 30 per kilo bolus in the department, piperacillin-tazobactam started within the hour. Repeat lactate every 6 hours until cleared, telemetry, strict intake and output, hold the lisinopril. Admit inpatient. I expect this admission to span at least two midnights: he needs 48 hours of intravenous antibiotics pending cultures, lactate clearance, and recovery of renal function before any oral step-down is safe.
Dentures labeled and placed in the denture cup at the bedside. Patient prefers them out at night. Oral care done.
Patient requested something for sleep. Melatonin 3 milligrams given per order at 2130. Slept in two-hour stretches per night shift report.
Pneumococcal vaccine status reviewed, up to date per state registry. Influenza vaccine offered and accepted, given left deltoid.
Potassium 3.5 this morning, repleted with 20 milliequivalents oral per protocol. Recheck with morning labs.
Overnight: vital signs every 2 hours, two episodes of rigors, warm blankets, acetaminophen given. Tolerating sips. Urine output recorded hourly.
Hospital day 2 labs. Lactate 2.1 at 12 hours. White count 15.0. Creatinine 1.9. Blood cultures: gram-negative rods in 2 of 2 bottles, identification pending.

Hospital day 2. Not an observation candidate: blood pressure dipped to 84 over 48 overnight requiring a third liter, lactate 2.6 at 6 hours and 2.1 at 12 hours, creatinine 1.9 this morning. Continue intravenous antibiotics and fluids, nephrology aware.
IV site rotated from the left forearm to the right hand, old site without redness. Dressing dated. Patient tolerated well.
Skin assessment on admission. Braden 15. Skin intact, no pressure injury, heels floated. Turn every two hours while in bed. Barrier cream to the sacrum as a precaution.
Social work met with the patient and his son to confirm the home address, the primary contact, and transportation for follow-up appointments. No barriers identified today.
Chaplain visited at the patient's request, about twenty minutes. He appreciated the visit. No needs identified.
Home omeprazole resumed at the home dose this morning after review with the attending. No interactions flagged.

Hospital day 3. Improving. Temperature maximum 37.9, heart rate 92, blood pressure 108 over 66 without fluids since this morning. Lactate 1.6. Creatinine 1.5. Cultures pending speciation. Advance diet, continue intravenous antibiotics.
Day 3 nursing. Ambulated in the hall with standby assistance twice, tolerating a regular diet, voiding without difficulty, pain 2 out of 10. Intravenous antibiotics infusing on schedule.
Bowel regimen started, senna and docusate at bedtime. Last bowel movement 2 days ago per patient. Encouraged fluids and ambulation as able.
Daily weight 176 pounds, up 2 from yesterday. Intake and output recorded. Repositioned per schedule, skin checked.
Fall risk assessment completed, score 60, high risk. Bed alarm on, nonskid socks, call light within reach, hourly rounding. Family at bedside this evening.
Hospital day 4. Afebrile 36 hours, lactate 1.1, creatinine back to 1.1, cultures grew E. coli sensitive to cefpodoxime. Discharged home on oral antibiotics.
Dietitian consult. Regular diet with heart healthy modification. Intake about 51 percent of meals. Supplement shake twice daily added. Will follow.
Pharmacy note. Renal dosing reviewed, creatinine 1.0, no adjustments needed today. Home medication list reconciled with the daughter by phone, one duplicate statin removed.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-1 (sepsis); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
